verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Coimbatore textile-machinery makers with confirmed order books and clean receivables; avoid mills-dependent job-work units until TN GST trend turns.
title: Coimbatore textile machinery: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Coimbatore's textile-machinery units build and service spinning, winding and processing machines for the mills around Coimbatore, Tiruppur and Pallipalayam. **Cash turns on a long cycle: order, build, dispatch, then retention and service receivables.** Value sits in the order book and after-sales service, not in the shed. Capex is moderate but lumpy; working capital is the real exposure. The ICRA fabric methodology notes weaving is fixed-capital and working-capital intensive, so funding needs run high [10]. ## What has changed now
Demand has revived. Peer LMW's textile machinery turnover rose 32% on the quarter to ₹639 crore, with an order book of about INR 34 billion [4][5]. But the local signal is weak: **Tamil Nadu GST collections are -3.2% Apr-to-date against India +6.1%** [D]. Bonus season is on, with some Tiruppur units speaking of slower orders [1]. ## Where to grow
Pursue component and sub-assembly suppliers feeding LMW-type OEMs, and service/retrofit firms that upgrade existing spindles — these ride the modernisation wave without owning the mill's risk [3][4]. **Avoid pure job-work units whose sole buyer is one stressed mill.** When a proposal lands, check the order book and buyer concentration; if one buyer exceeds half of sales, ask for the purchase order and payment history. ## How to grow safely
Structure term loans to match the machine-build cycle, not the mill's. **Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements and quarterly GST returns** — the state's -3.2% GST trend [D] means you verify turnover yourself. Covenant a debt-service cover and cap total outside liabilities; ICRA flags that heavy debt reliance makes such units more vulnerable in downturns [10]. ## Early-warning signs
Watch receivable days stretching beyond the stated credit period, inventory build without matching orders, and bonus payment delays at the borrower's mill customers [1]. **If a borrower's top buyer defers payment twice, freeze fresh limits and inspect the shop floor.**
